No.09

How to View High Housing Prices and Unhappiness?

Facing the weight of meals, rent and daily life — first care for survival, then settle the heart.

Author's record · translated; the Chinese original is authoritative

Open in reading mode →

🔶Inquiry to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

How does the Bodhisattva see people who toil and rush for money and live without any happiness? And how do you see land and house prices in Taiwan soaring so high that people cannot see hope for the future? Could you give some advice?

🔶The Bodhisattva's Teaching

Most people labor for food and clothing; labor long, and they forget their original heart. They run after profit; run long, and they lose their peace. The fault is not in money, but in the heart that takes money as its very life. Houses in this world were meant to shelter from wind and rain; now they store greed, store fear, store unease. So the buildings rise high while hearts sink low; prices soar while hopes wither. The land is not evil, the people are not foolish; it is the shared karma of many hearts that has taken this form.

If the heart only seeks outward, there will never be a day of peace;
if the heart can turn and look within, every place is a path.
Do not ask when the world will be at peace;
ask only whether your heart has a place to drop anchor.

🔶Plain Rendering

People today constantly rush about for food and clothing, and over time they forget the heart they started with; worn out from chasing profit, in the end they have no peace left inside.

Money itself is not to blame. The trouble is that people treat money as the root of their life, so that whenever it runs short, life feels as if it has nothing to lean on.

Houses were meant to keep out wind and rain, but now they have become places that hold greed, fear and unease.

So the buildings grow taller while people's hearts grow lower; house prices climb higher while people's hopes wither day by day.

The land is not evil and the people are not foolish; today's hardship is the karmic force created together by countless people's thoughts.

If you only look outward, you will never find a steady day;

if you can come back and look into your own heart, then wherever you are, there is a path where you can settle your life.

Do not ask when the world will be at peace; just ask yourself whether your heart already has something real to rely on, a place to rest.

🔶Inquiry to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

I replied to the Bodhisattva: you say not to be enslaved by money, but many people cannot even pay for three meals, rent, the mortgage or their children's expenses. How can they not be enslaved by money?

🔶The Bodhisattva's Teaching

When beings are pressed by hunger and cold,
it is not their greed, but their suffering.
When I say "do not be a slave to money",
I do not teach you to throw money away;
I teach you: "Do not let money become the root of your life."
If you have no rice, first seek rice;
if you have no home, first seek a home;
this is not attachment, it is right livelihood.

But most people grow afraid when they lack,
grow greedy when afraid,
and lose themselves when greedy.
You ask how not to be a slave to money?
I answer in a few words: first settle the body, then settle the heart.

🔶Plain Rendering

When people suffer from hunger and cold, that is real suffering, not greed at work. When I say "do not be a slave to money", I do not mean ignoring money altogether, but rather: "Do not treat money as the only root of your life." If you have no rice, first look for rice; if you have no home, first look for a home; this is a reasonable effort to survive, not attachment. But most people become afraid when they lack, become greedy out of fear, and lose themselves in greed. How can you truly not be a slave to money? These few words are enough: first settle the body, then settle the heart.
